sources.citation: Azeb Amha, James Slotta & Hannah S. Sarvasy. 2021. Singing the individual: name tunes in Oyda and Yopno. Frontiers in Psychology 12: 667599. doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2021.667599
sources.note: Nothing on Oyda word stress, accent or lexical tone; only classification (Ometo branch of Omotic, c. 45,000 speakers) and the whistled/sung moyze name-tune system (the 'non-tonal' remark in the paper is about Yopno, not Oyda).

sources.citation: Hirut Woldemariam. 2010. Oyda language. In Siegbert Uhlig (ed.), Encyclopaedia Aethiopica, vol. 4 (O-X), 83-84. Wiesbaden: Harrassowitz.
sources.note: Nothing. The phonology paragraph lists the consonant inventory (stops, ejectives, implosives, sibilants, affricates, nasals, liquids, glides, glottals), a five-vowel system i e a o u, and 'Major phonological processes in O. include assimilation, insertion, deletion and vowel harmony'; no word on stress, accent or tone. Lit. cites Haile Eyesus Engdashet, A Descriptive Grammar of Oyda, Addis Ababa 2003 (ms.).

sources.citation: DoBeS 'Oyda' documentation project web pages (language / project / team / data examples), MPI Nijmegen; team Azeb Amha, Rainer Vossen, Bernhard Koehler, Hirut Woldemariam, Jan Abbink.
sources.note: No prose on prosody. Language page says the only materials are wordlists, Haileyesus Engedashet 2002 (case) and Abraham Dilnesaw 2003 (MA); project page promises a sketch grammar. Data page gives acute-marked citation forms (ʔáde 'father', ʔíndó 'mother', kéets 'house', landá 'bird', lamʔí 'two', pétto 'one', mins'á 'tree') whose accent position varies lexically, but this is transcription only, not a statement.
